title: 'I left my girl in the mountain' and the Boston burglar
summary: Nash recalls a railroad singer's song about leaving a girl in the mountains, a Georgia sheriff shooting and a chain gang, and sings it; the Boston burglar was already recorded.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: Do you want to record one of them, Forrest? I might get one of them.
I might get one of them. Yeah, I know the fellow who sang that sad song on the railroad about my home in Boston City Boys. Home in Boston City Boys.
Yeah, another guy, yeah. He sang that song about I left my girl in the mountain.
Well, sing the one. We already got the Boston burglar. Let's sing the other one.

Oh, I left my girl in the mountain? Yeah. He used to sing that song. I left my girl in the mountain, Standing out in the rain. I walked out to that freight shop, And caught myself a midnight train. I get swayed down in Georgia. I guess down in the gambling town. Boys, I've got in trouble. I shot a county sheriff down. Well, they put me on board that eastbound train, On the cold December day. Boys, every town that I went to, Could hear those people say. Down to go that Georgie mother. They got him with a ball and chain. Oh, oh boy, I'll never see my girl again. There stood my great mother, Her tears come rolling down. My son, my son, what?
